title: Design a Circular Queue
statement:
Design a circular queue: a first-in, first-out queue that keeps its values in a fixed row of `k` slots. The slot after the last one is the first one again, so the space a `dequeue` frees at the front can be used by a later `enqueue` at the back. Write a `CircularQueue` class, built from `k`, with six operations:

- `enqueue x` adds `x` at the back and returns `true`, or returns `false` when the queue is full.
- `dequeue` removes the value at the front and returns `true`, or returns `false` when the queue is empty.
- `front` returns the value at the front, or `-1` when the queue is empty.
- `rear` returns the value at the back, or `-1` when the queue is empty.
- `isEmpty` returns `true` when the queue holds no values, and `false` otherwise.
- `isFull` returns `true` when the queue holds `k` values, and `false` otherwise.

Every operation should take the same short time however full the queue is, so don't shift values along the row. The first line is `k`, at least 1. The second line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to every operation on its own line. Values are whole numbers from 0 to 1000.

Input:

```text
3
10
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
enqueue 3
enqueue 4
rear
isFull
dequeue
enqueue 4
rear
front
```

Expected output:

```text
true
true
true
false
3
true
true
true
4
2
```

hints: Keep the row of `k` slots, the index of the front value, and how many values the queue holds. Those three numbers answer every operation.
The back of the queue sits `size` slots after the front. Wrap an index past the end with `% k`, so slot `k` becomes slot 0.
A dequeue doesn't need to clear its slot. Moving the front index forward by one (and wrapping) is enough, since that slot now counts as free.
